_comment: Bean tyo0 (#1767). One agent's INSPECTION of every image extracted from the three WHO Digital Transformation Handbook uploads ingested into smart-base/library on 2026-10-01, as data rather than code (bean d5f1). Every entry was produced by looking at the image, with the page text for captions. `saw` is the reason for the role; `draft` is the description, applied as a DRAFT narrative that only a person may confirm (bun run cat narratives). Notable judgements a reviewer may want to revisit: supply-chain img-p019-1 may be the Principles for Digital Development mark (left decorative, unconfirmed); the icons inside its Fig. 30 are decorative because each sits beside a text label that carries the meaning; the reference architecture's two most-repeated images (img-p001-1, img-p019-1) are fully transparent placeholders under the DRAFT watermark; and that draft captions two different figures 'Figure 3.5' (pp. 63 and 77), kept as the document has it. | Bean ay3x (2026-10-03): `vfig-pNNN` entries judge the VECTOR renders pdf-vector-figures.py writes to <entry>/figures/, applied to vector-figures.json by the same script. Each carries its own inspected_by/inspected_at because two of these documents already hold another session's raster verdicts, and `shows` names the declared figures the render holds — the only thing image-descriptions credits. They were judged against the BARE figures (no raster image, no caption text) specifically: every render whose page names a bare figure was looked at.
